title: Valid Anagram
description: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` can be formed by rearranging the letters of `s` (using every letter exactly as many times as it appears), and `false` otherwise.

examples.explanation: Both strings contain the same letters with the same counts.

constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters
hints: If the lengths differ the answer is immediately false. Otherwise, what must be true about how often each letter appears?
Two strings are anagrams exactly when their letter counts match. Which structure can hold 26 counters?
Count letters of `s` upward and letters of `t` downward (or compare two counters); any non-zero leftover means false.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def isAnagram(self, s: str, t: str) -> bool:

solution.explanation: Anagrams have identical letter frequencies. Count each letter of `s`, subtract the letters of `t`, and check every count ends at zero (after first rejecting different lengths). This is one pass over each string, O(n) time, and the counter has at most 26 keys, so space is O(1). Sorting both strings and comparing works too in O(n log n).
